name: issue_623_debounce_race_transient_open_not_paused
description: A monitored sensor whose raw HA state already reads open, but whose debounce-timer registration hasn't run yet (the exact scheduling race between an unrelated coordinator refresh and the state-changed event listener), must NOT be treated as settled-open — the routine comfort-restore path must wait for the debounce window, not pause instantly (Issue #623)
notes: Occupant impact: on 2026-08-11 the user exited through a door at 15:29 and got an instant
'HVAC paused' notification, even though the project's sensor-debounce mechanism exists
specifically to ignore momentary/transient opens (e.g. walking in or out). This bypassed
the entire 10-minute debounce window the user configured, and cascaded into a grace-period
start/expire/re-pause sequence and a second comfort-violation incident less than an hour
later -- all downstream of the false-positive pause.
Root cause (Issue #620 regression, PR #621/commit b6843ca): Fix A
(_sync_paused_by_door_with_live_sensors()) reads live raw sensor state via
_any_monitored_sensor_open() and only defers via _sensor_debounce_pending, which used to
mean 'is a timer currently registered in _door_open_timers'. That timer is only populated
inside _async_door_window_changed(), the state-changed EVENT LISTENER. Because HA state
reads (hass.states.get()) reflect a fresh transition immediately, but our own listener is
scheduled as a separate coroutine, an unrelated periodic coordinator refresh cycle can win
the race and read 'open, not debounce-pending' before the listener has registered the
timer for that exact transition -- exactly matching the incident's log: the pause fired at
15:29:46.907/.910, 5ms BEFORE 'Contact sensor opened ... debounce started' logged at .912
for the same sensor.
Fix: _sensor_debounce_pending (coordinator.py) now also checks each open sensor's own
HA-authoritative last_changed timestamp -- set by HA's state machine at the physical
transition instant, independent of when our listener coroutine gets scheduled -- in
addition to the existing _door_open_timers registry check.
Scenario design: the sensor_open event uses seed_fresh (not seed) -- silently sets the
sensor 'on' via the harness's set_simple() (no listener dispatch, so _door_open_timers
stays empty, faithfully modeling the race where the listener hasn't run) but stamps a
fresh last_changed via the sim clock, faithfully modeling 'raw state already reflects the
open, timestamp says it JUST happened'. A classification cycle immediately after must NOT
pause -- the sensor is well within the configured 10-minute debounce window.
Three-exercise protocol (CLAUDE.md Sec 10):
(a) Scenario effectiveness: reverting _sensor_debounce_pending() to the old
'lambda: bool(self._door_open_timers)' makes this scenario fail -- the classification
cycle immediately after seed_fresh would see debounce_pending=False (no timer
registered) and pause instantly. Verified via revert-test before promoting.
(b) Docs-production alignment: docs/grace-periods-spec.md's _sensor_debounce_pending note
(added for #620) is updated to describe the last_changed-based check and why
(Issue #623 doc pass).
(c) User outcome: briefly opening/exiting through a monitored door no longer produces an
instant pause notification and grace-period cascade -- the debounce window the user
configured is actually honored.

events.note: Hot afternoon: indoor at the comfort ceiling, outdoor far above -- no free-cooling eligibility, isolates the debounce-race check from nat-vent logic entirely (fan_mode=disabled).
Normal classification applies cool@74F -- sensor closed, nothing to pause for.
Models the exact race: raw state now reads open, but no debounce timer registered yet -- matching the real incident's 5ms window before 'debounce started' was logged.

A routine classification cycle fires 1 second later -- exactly the unrelated periodic refresh that won the race in production. Must NOT pause: the sensor is 1 second into a 600-second debounce window.

assertions.reason: First classification applies normally -- no sensor open yet.

Issue #623: even though the sensor's raw state already reads open and _door_open_timers is empty (listener hasn't run), _sensor_debounce_pending() must recognize the sensor is only 1 second into its 600-second debounce window via last_changed, and apply_classification() must proceed normally -- not pause. The debounce mechanism exists precisely to ignore a transient/fresh open like this.

verdict.summary: A sensor whose raw state just changed but whose debounce timer hasn't registered yet is still correctly treated as pending, not settled -- classification proceeds normally instead of pausing instantly (Issue #623)
verdict.observed_behavior: classification_applied (cool@74F) -> sensor opens with a fresh timestamp but no registered timer -> next classification cycle -> classification_applied again, HVAC unaffected
verdict.expected_behavior: The debounce window is honored even when the internal timer-registry hasn't caught up with a fresh raw-state transition
